It takes a lot of courage and self-awareness to recognize this pattern and want to change it. Possessiveness often stems from underlying fears, such as a fear of abandonment, deep-seated insecurities, or past betrayals. When you feel that possessive urge rising, it can be helpful to pause and ask yourself what specific fear is being triggered in that moment. Recognizing that these feelings are usually about your own internal worries, rather than your friends' actions, is a crucial first step toward changing the dynamic.

To truly work through these root causes, consider speaking with a mental health professional. A therapist can provide a safe space to explore where these fears originated and help you develop healthier coping mechanisms and attachment styles. In the meantime, being honest with your friends about your struggles can help. Letting them know you are aware of your behavior and are actively working on it can foster understanding and patience while you focus on healing.
